newsitem.title: USA: Beer companies tell government about ad buys.
newsitem.headline: Beer companies tell government about ad buys.

text.p: Anheuser-Busch Cos. Inc. and Miller Brewing Co., the nation's two largest brewers, said Monday they had provided the Federal Trade Commission with information on their ad purchases.
Anheuser-Busch, the No. 1 brewer, denied its ads target young people.
Advertising Age reported Monday the FTC had contacted Anheuser Busch and and Miller for information on ad placements on MTV, which is watched by young people.
"We do not target our advertising toward young people," period," Stephen Lambright, vice president of Anheuser-Busch, said in a statement from St. Louis.

"We have not received a subpoena or official notification regarding and FTC investigation," the statement said, adding the brewer had "proactively contacted the agency and volunteered to provide them information on our overall media buying practices. The FTC took us up on our offer."
A spokeswoman for Miller, a unit of Philip Morris Cos. Inc., said the company received a request Jan. 14 for information on its media buys.
"We sent information as requested and are co-operating fully," said Susan Henderson in Milwaukee.

Earlier this year, Advertising Age reported the two beer companies ran ads on MTV in time slots where at least half the audience was below the legal drinking age. Anheuser-Busch pulled its ads in December and Miller said it has required that its ads run in later time slots, the report said.
A spokeswoman for the FTC said the agency could not confirm or deny ongoing investigations.

President Clinton has made hard liquor ads on television a focus of his administration, especially in light of possible influence on the young. But he contacted the Federal Communications Commission instead of the FTC, which has jurisdiction over advertising.
